_meta.recallFanoutRemoved: **Corrected 2026-10-05.** `recall.fanout` was removed from this file, from `C0` and `C1`, and from the policy itself (`packages/core/src/types.ts`, `AssemblyPolicy.recall`; `packages/core/src/config.ts`, `LEGACY_POLICY_KEYS`). It was `k`, the per-node expansion fanout of the recall walk - each BFS node expanded at most its k heaviest neighbours - and the line this preset carried read `"fanout": 8`. It is gone because it was **never in the originating brief** (the prompt mentions it zero times; the brief bounds recall with `recall.depth` and `recall.threshold` only, plus `recall.window`, which it says exists only to save System-1 calls and must not affect recall), **in no record** (the tape's `kind:"wiring"` record carries `recall: {d, r, w, wait, tier1}` and no k, so the authority this file's `provider` note points at never carried the field), and **in no panel** (the plugin's `Tuning` fields are depth, relevanceThreshold, window, anchorWaitMs and tracePlacement) - so a parameter that decided behaviour lived only here, where the project says the authority is not. **The earlier justification for it was wrong, and that is measured.** It was kept on the argument that without k a depth-2 walk reaches essentially the whole graph and makes `depth` meaningless; that arithmetic used the mean edge degree to derive `1 + 37.6 + 37.6^2 = 1450 > 228` segments, and ignored the rule that every step goes into a segment earlier in the append order. Walking from **every** segment as anchor on `round-20261004-1239`'s frozen graph, backwards-only, at depth 2, the reachable sets under `k = 8` and under an unbounded k are identical for **63.2 %** of anchors (they differ for 84 of 228). **What the round it was measured in recorded: no number of that round changes with the removal.** In that round the walk returned `candidates = 0` from invocation 9 onward, because the System-1 lane was 4.6x too slow to score the pairs and the tail therefore had no edges, so `fanout` had no effect on anything the round wrote - the removal changes the design, not that round's data. The rounds that did record a non-empty walk (`20261004-0233`, `20261004-1211`) stay readable and unedited: the field is gone from the policy, and a preset or profile that still writes it is read and reported rather than dropped in silence. **What replaced it, and what the removal costs:** `recall.threshold` - the brief's own knob, and the one that is in the settings panel. On the 36.8 % of anchors where the cap did bite, the uncapped walk selects **more** segments (median **+27**, worst **+69**), so the `recalled` block can grow on those steps; lowering `r` is how a round asks for a smaller block. The two cannot be converted into one another - k counted neighbours expanded per node and `r` drops candidate edges by relevance - so a round re-tunes the block size rather than translating the old number.
_meta.note: **Corrected 2026-10-05, and the superseded wording is carried here because this note is a record.** It read: "The project's own configuration: TAS on, recall selection on (`tier1: s1`, the implemented mode), x first; `xFirst: true` and `deliver: true` come from `cellPolicy('C2')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) and are not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell." The project's own configuration, restated with the fields the build has: TAS on, recall selection on (`tier1: s1`, the implemented mode), and the paper's arrangement - the question last (not a field: `questionPlacement` was **deleted** on 2026-10-05, because the paper fixes `q` last in every condition, so `q` is now the last block of every recorded order by construction), and the trace in front of the long context (`tracePlacement`; code-owned and absent from this file). An old profile spelling is still read and reported (`LEGACY_LAYOUT_KEYS` in packages/core/src/config.ts): question-last spellings are warned about as retired and harmless, question-first ones are refused with the sentence that retired them. **Why the rename:** the paper places the question last in every condition (arXiv:2609.02702 section 4.1) and its two arms are `[T, x, q]` (Trace as State) and `[x, T, q]` (Trace Append) with order the only difference - `xFirst` moved the question, the one element the paper fixes, and its name presented that as the paper's variable. **Evidence:** round `20261004-0233`'s own `layoutOrder` records - this cell recorded `pinned, stateProxy, anchor, recalled, tail`, the question second, which is neither paper arm, while `C0` recorded `pinned, recalled, tail, anchor`. `deliver: true` comes from `cellPolicy('C2')` and is not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell. **Registration changed 2026-10-04.** It used to read: the contrast the registered rule tests is this cell against `C0`, the baseline, because `C1` was a second control arm that delivered nothing, so no effect of this arm could be read from a C1-vs-C2 difference. That reason is gone - the delivery channel now sends the trace, so `C1` delivers `T` alone and this cell delivers `T` plus recall selection. The registered contrasts are now **`C0 -> C1`** (what the trace's presence buys, System-1 lane absent) and **`C1 -> C2`** (what this cell's recall selection buys on top); the endpoint test in docs/FORMULAS.md §8 is still C0 against C2, and the statement of record is the comment above `cellPolicy()`. What is still NOT measurable in either step is the paper's variable, which is the trace's POSITION: delivery appends and renders T before the recalled block by construction, so `policy.tracePlacement` - the enforced axis naming the paper's two orders since 2026-10-05, where the old `stateProxyPosition` composed with a boolean `xFirst` that moved the question instead - reaches the recorded `layout.order` and not the delivered text, and the model-view write-back that would deliver a layout rather than a block remains a separate project (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, `packages/proxy`). **Corrected 2026-10-05 (the recalled block's position - appended, because this note is a record).** The recalled block now sits immediately before the anchor, behind the tail: this cell's recorded order is the TAS row of the table in `packages/core/src/assembler.ts`'s header, and `AssemblyLayout.order` (`packages/core/src/types.ts`) is the statement of record for it. It used to be third of five, with `tail` and `anchor` behind it. That is a move *inside* the paper's long context `x`, not a move of the paper's variable: the variable is where `T` sits relative to `x`, and this cell's arm is unchanged, because `T` is still ahead of every block of `x` under `trace-as-state`. The sentence above about what is and is not measurable is unaffected in the same way - the move changes the recorded `layout.order` and the cache arithmetic that reads it, not the delivered text: `T` is still rendered before the recalled turns by construction, so the model still reads `[..., x, T, recalled, ...]`. **Why it moved:** prompt caching is prefix caching, so anything placed behind a block that changes every step is invalidated with it, and the recalled block is the block a re-selection moves. Measured on round `20261004-1458` C2: the whole-prompt invalidation span per delivered pair fell from 2,539 to 2,111 tokens with this move, on top of the ordering change that had already cut it from 6,179 to 2,539. The round record quoted above (round `20261004-0233` recorded this cell's order) is that round's own data and is left as written, and no value in this file changed with any of this.
_meta.tier1: `recall.tier1` is `s1` here, and it said `embed` until 2026-10-02 - a mode with no implementation, read in the whole codebase by exactly one test, `policy.recall.tier1 !== 'off'` (packages/core/src/assembler.ts). No embedder exists, `source: 'embed'` is never assigned to an edge, and the round's own graph snapshot says which scorers ran: `s1-noul` 1 824 edges, `lexical` 253 976, embed **0**. So the cell named a mechanism it does not use while a reader could only find out by grepping; `s1` is the mode that runs (one batched `noul` call). A literal `embed` is now rejected by `validatePolicy` with its own message rather than treated as "not off" (packages/core/src/config.ts, `LEGACY_TIER1`), and `recall.embedModel` - which nothing reads - is warned about when it is non-empty. The tier-1 *axis* of the design remains unmeasured: implementing the embed mode is what would measure it, and that is a separate project, not a rename.
_meta.planGateRemoved: This file carried `planGate: { on: true, ... }` until 2026-10-02, and round `20261002-2037` is why it no longer does. That round - the one this cell was written for - contains **zero** `plan_gate` records: not in its control plane (6 546 records), not on its tape (2 003 lines), not in its session stream, across 277 steps and 289 tool calls. The gate can be reached in exactly two ways, a numbered or bulleted plan in an assistant message (`extractPlans`) or a `todo/write` session event (`extractTodoEvent`), and that run produced neither: the model wrote prose and reasoning, and the event stream carries no `todo/write` at all. So the arm advertised an ordering step it never ran, in the one cell whose whole purpose is to be the full configuration. The knob is removed rather than given a new path, because adding one would change what C2 *is* mid-study - a new plan source means new System-1 calls, and the C1-vs-C2 comparison the file's own `note` rests on would no longer be between the two cells that were run. Nothing takes over the gate's role: the honest reading of round `20261002-2037` is that C2's ordering half was TAS alone, exactly as in C1, and the difference between the two arms was recall selection. `packages/core/src/types.ts` carries the full decision; the mechanism itself (`packages/core/src/plan-gate.ts`, `packages/dsh-plugin/src/plan-gate-runtime.ts`) is kept and still tested for whichever arm next has a plan source the model actually writes to. Two clauses of that record were overtaken on 2026-10-02 and are corrected here rather than rewritten: the C1-vs-C2 comparison this file's `note` used to rest on is no longer the registration (the contrast is C0 vs C2, and `C1` is a second control that delivers nothing - see `C1.json`'s `_meta.secondControl` - and a further clause was overtaken on 2026-10-04, when `C1` was re-opened as the paper's arm and the contrasts became `C0 -> C1` and `C1 -> C2`), and "the difference between the two arms was recall selection" is true of what reached the model only in the sense that C2's one delivery channel inserts recalled turns: the ordering half reached the model in neither arm, which is why the ordering claim this cell's role names is not measurable until the model-view write-back exists.
_meta.retry: `s1.retryAttempts: 2` is set below per docs/CELLS-RUN.md's setup, and this cell needs it most: C2 makes an order of magnitude more System-1 calls than the other two arms, the shared Laya refuses rather than queues at its admission limit, and a measured round lost 732 of 2 016 calls to `503 server busy` - a refused call falls back to the local lexical scorer, so an unrecovered refusal turns an S1-governed cell into a partly lexical one. The retry waits the server's own `Retry-After` and is answered, and `attempts`/`waitedMs` on the `s1_call` record report how often it was needed; report `judgedPairs / scoredPairs` either way.
_meta.admissionLimit: `s1.admissionLimit: 2` - it read `8` until 2026-10-05, and the paragraph below is that value's reasoning, which the measurement left standing while the number moved. It is the other half of the same problem `retryAttempts` addresses. A retry is the right answer to *one* refusal; it is the wrong answer to a backend refusing everything, because the retry is one more request inside the same admission window. Round `20261002-2037` measured what that costs: 5 992 `s1_call` records over a 2 219.7 s span - **2.70 requests/second** - of which **3 859 (64.4 %)** were refused with `503 {"detail":"server busy"}`, the refusal rate above a third in every thirty-second bucket of the run, 4 057 of them carrying `attempts: 2` and 4 057 000 ms of `waitedMs` between them, for a yield of `judgedPairs / scoredPairs = 4 152 / 860 672 = 0.48 %`. The local Laya admits 16 concurrent requests and refuses the rest; one cell saturated it by itself, because the upkeep queue drains several events per tick without awaiting its async handler, so several scoring loops were in flight at once. The plugin now caps what this cell may have in flight at this number and opens a circuit breaker after a run of refusals, probing once per cooldown until the backend answers again. A window the gate does not send is **deferred**, not scored lexically: the graph holds its cursor over it, the pair is not counted in `scoredPairs`, and it is counted in `deferredPairs` on the assembly record instead - so `judgedPairs / scoredPairs` stays the share of what was offered that the backend answered, and the omission is a number with a reason rather than a lower coverage nobody can see. **Why the number moved, 2026-10-05.** Three measurements, none of which the `8` had. (a) On the live backend, throughput is **flat** in concurrency - 8.23 / 8.25 / 8.25 / 8.21 / 8.21 questions/s at in-flight 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 - while wall latency is **linear**, p50 2.43 s at one and 17.06 s at sixteen. A slot past the first therefore buys queue depth and no work: the cap was bounding nothing it was meant to bound. (b) The same curve reaches **p95 = 39 s at in-flight 16**, against the client's transport guard, so the upper end of this cap manufactures the very `S1TimeoutError` the `retry` note above is about. (c) Most importantly, this cell's own round `20261004-0233` was **paid 4.45 times** for the same work: 9,828 questions asked for **2,211 distinct pairs** (`scores` held exactly `67*66/2` rows), because several sweeps started at once shared one cursor and walked it backwards as well as forwards. `AssociationGraph.scoreNew` now claims each entry **before its first `await`**, so L in flight finally means L *distinct* segments and this number means what the gate promises. **Pre-registered, because it will look like a regression:** a lower limit moves the *first* refusal **earlier**, so `deferredPairs` and the deferred share read **larger** at the same instant while the graph fills faster - `deferredPairs` is a tail counted once from the first refusal, not a rate, and no pair is lost. Judge this change by **distinct pairs settled per GPU-second**, not by the deferral share.
_meta.provider: **Corrected 2026-10-05 (2).** `s1.provider` is `jev` again, the **remote** System-1 service at `https://api.typesafe.ai`, and this time the key exists: `GET /v1/models` lists `jev-latest` and `jev-preview`, and a live probe of `POST /v1/systemone` from this machine answered **20 `noul` questions in one round trip in 323 ms** (single question 291 ms warm, 688 ms cold; server model `jev-1.13.0`; 1 821 input / 355 output tokens for the batch). The lane separates: candidates cycling relevant / changelog / relevant-test / README came back **0.81 0.11 0.81 0.04** repeating, so the relevant two land at 0.81-0.83 and the irrelevant two at 0.03-0.11, and `r = 0.58` cuts in the empty band between them. `s1.model` is stated below rather than inherited from the provider matrix, for the reason this whole file exists: the file is the source, and the record reads the value from it. The note this replaces said the value "previously read `jev` ... which would additionally have needed an API key it does not have" — that was true when it was written and is not true now. **The reasoning below is kept because it is the record of why the field went to `laya-serve` in the first place.** It is `laya-serve`, the **local** backend at `http://127.0.0.1:8008`, and the live per-cell profile pins `s1.baseUrl` to that address (docs/CELLS-RUN.md's setup) - so the value here has to be the one the profile overrides it with, or the file describes a lane no cell uses. What a cell actually ran is recorded, and can be re-read, from its own `kind:"wiring"` tape record - `verify-wiring.mjs` asserts it - so treat that record, not this file, as the authority.
_meta.recallThreshold: `recall.threshold` is **0.58** from 2026-10-05 (round 3 of the day); it read `0.6` for round `20261004-1618` and `0.55` before that, and both superseded values are named here because this file is a record. **The user set it, and the measurement is why.** Round `20261004-1618` ran at `0.60` and its own activity matrix shows the consequence: of 2 604 recorded cells, **41 were walk candidates** and none was a delivered selection — the walk became so sparse that 9 of 21 invocations returned `cand = 0`, and the recency fallback (`recall.minRecalledSegments: 1`) then delivered **387 of that round's 480 delivered segments (81 %)** on a path that does not consult `r` at all. `0.58` is the step between the two measured ends, and the live Jev probe says where the gap is: relevant candidates score 0.81-0.83 and irrelevant ones 0.03-0.11, so anything in 0.20-0.80 separates them, and the choice inside that band is about how much of the *distribution* rather than the *separation* is kept. **The distribution the earlier choice was made on is still the number to read beside it.** On round `20261004-1458` (C2 alone, `w = 16`, `N = 170`, all 2,584 offered pairs scored) the `noul` weights over every scored pair ran min 0.344, p10 0.484, p25 0.519, **p50 0.547**, p75 0.572, p90 0.600, max 0.743 — so **`0.55` sat on the median**, exactly half of all pairs became edges, the edge density was 46.4 % and the mean degree 14.1 out of the 16 the window allows. That is a nearly complete graph, not a selection, and it is why that round's activity matrix shows the walk over-reaching. The same sweep: `0.50` -> 2,189 edges / 84.7 % / degree 25.8; **`0.55` -> 1,198 / 46.4 % / 14.1**; `0.60` -> 252 / 9.8 % / 3.0; `0.65` -> 20 / 0.8 % / 0.2; `0.70` -> 4 / 0.2 %; `0.75` and above -> none. **That sweep is a local-Laya measurement and the Jev band is wider** (0.11 against 0.83 rather than a 0.12-wide band from p10 to p90), so `0.58` here is not the same selectivity it would have been on the local lane; the round's own record is what says which it was. Two things this is not. It is **not** a deviation from the brief — `r` is the brief's own knob (`recall.threshold = r`, 0 <= r <= 1, named to state its meaning). And it is **not** a precise instrument. **It also multiplies with the on-demand scoring landed the same day.** Measured on that round's frozen graph at its own anchors, lazy scoring saves 3.1 % of the pairs at `r = 0.55` and **63.6 % at `r = 0.60`** (66 rows / 941 pairs against eager's 169 / 2,584), because a walk that spreads less demands fewer rows. So this value is not only a recall-quality choice: it is the parameter the System-1 lane's cost now turns on most.
_meta.recallWindowInherited: `recall.window` is NOT set in this file on purpose, and it is **16** since 2026-10-05 (`defaultPolicy()`, packages/core/src/types.ts; the validator's floor moved 64 -> 4 in the same change). `cellPolicy('C2')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) starts from `defaultPolicy()` and sets `recall.tier1: 's1'`; it moves neither the window nor the depth, so the window reaches this cell from the default with nothing here to override it. `depth` IS carried explicitly above (16 since 2026-10-05, it read 2): this is the one cell that runs the walk, so its depth is the value a reader compares against the round. **This is the cell the measurement was taken in** - round `20261004-1239`, 228 segments, the lane measured at 16.1 questions/s (5,958 questions in 369.2 s) - and the cost is in `docs/FORMULAS.md` section "Recall window w": `w = 1024` offered all 25,878 pairs (`sum_{i=1}^{227} min(i, w)`) and needed 26.7 min of lane against a 6.2 min session, so the window bought nothing and the tail had no edges; `w = 16` offers 3,512 (14 %) and fits in 3.6 min. What a bounded walk then reaches is `w x d` = 16 x 16 = **256** segments, against the 1024 x 2 = 2,048 the old pair gave - a shorter reach, bought deliberately, with `d` the knob that buys it back and the knob whose increase costs the lane nothing (the pair count contains no `d`). Rounds recorded at `w = 1024, d = 2` (`20261004-0233`, `1211`, `1239` and earlier, the last two with `fanout: 8`) stay readable and unedited: this file is a preset for the next round, and a round's own `kind:"wiring"` record is the authority on what it ran.
